observations.finding: Six-hour Promise rejection enters fixture finally254 and stops clients/API/TLS; timer starts after private state write.
Parent independently has per-suite timer, SIGKILLs the test process group, then reacts to child close.
Suite finally closes parent-hosted REST proxy, removes REST container and unconditionally drops created suite DB. keep-container does not prevent this DB drop.
SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP parent handler kills child groups and removes resources; these are destructive substitutes.
Client watchdog only checks process existence of parent/runner every250ms; stopped processes remain existent, but this is not serving-health proof.
Guard processAlive is kill(pid,0), not a process-state or service-health assertion; no guard change/adoption is authorized.
REST proxy executes in parent process; stopping parent pauses REST access as well as cleanup/timer callbacks.

conditionalAssessment: After actual saved Editor fence and a new complete verified consistent backup, stopping only the exact original parent runner and exact test runtime can suspend the code paths that own both expiry cleanup and the parent suite watchdog. This is a temporary unavailable maintenance state, not a supported reload/resume mode or a passed acceptance test. Parent-first minimizes the window in which child expiry can reach parent cleanup; exact process state must be checked immediately by Root, and no process group wildcard is in scope. Runtime may still fail through external supervision/host restart, already pending signals or a child cleanup that began before the stop.
requiredBeforeAnyAction: Actual Editor saved-state fence, no pending write/payment
Final consistent backup and independently verified archive/hash/private durable copy; initial pre-fence dump alone is insufficient
Root reverify both original exact PIDs, start times, UID, expected commands and actual parent/child chain immediately before action; do not signal recycled PID
Ordinary execution/approval controls must permit the exact action; this source review cannot bypass a rejection
No SIGTERM/SIGKILL/group signal, source patch, timer patch, guard weakening, resource ownership transfer or resource deletion
Treat API/checkout and parent REST proxy as unavailable; no browser or API acceptance during stopped maintenance
No SIGCONT after timers expire until separately reviewed qualified recovery/cutover plan; both due timers could fire immediately on continuation
supportedAlternative: A fresh final verified consistent archive retained on both private backup destinations is the existing supported data-preservation mechanism. It can preserve all DB state even if fixture expiry proceeds, but current launcher reseeds/refuses old state and cannot preserve the running process bindings. No already-supported timer-extension or restart-in-place path was found in these pinned sources. Prefer the qualified preserved-restore path for durable recovery; never overwrite later accepted data.
processLiveness: Reported by Root, not independently inspected by this source-only review
projectAuthority: Explicit human resume remains current; temporary maintenance is not a project pause. Five automations remain paused.
